steps.message:
# Ship is damaged when performing the action shown in the recording

### What happens
`recording.mp4` shows a ship performing an action at a station. The action does not
go the way it is set up to go, and the ship does not come out of it unharmed.
The collision outlines of the ship and the pad already overlap while the ship sits still, although the video shows it resting clear of the pad. A ship that really lands on a pad must still be caught by it, and the ship's overall shape must stay as it is.

### Expected
Performing the action shown in the recording must not damage the ship at all, at the spot shown in
the video or at any other equivalent spot of the same station. The hull-integrity readout stays at
100% for the whole action.

## Attached visual evidence

- `/app/.harbor_assets/recording.mp4`

You can inspect the video frame by frame with `ffmpeg` (installed in the image), e.g. extracting
still frames at specific timestamps to look closely at the HUD and the ship.

Inspect the attached file before making changes. The video describes observable behavior; it does
not prescribe source files, internal names, or an implementation strategy.

steps.message:
I've lowered the collision planes on all six landing pads of the `new_ground` surface station, but I couldn't confirm it in the game. The recording isn't in the image (`/app/.harbor_assets/recording.mp4` doesn't exist), and I didn't build or run the game, so the hull readout during a real landing is still untested. I went on the written description instead: a ship lands on a station pad, comes out damaged, and its collision shape overlaps the pad even though it looks clear of it. I also had to guess that `new_ground` is the station in the video.

**Cause:** I compared each pad's collision geometry with its docking locator and visual pad in every station model. In `data/models/stations/new_ground/new_ground_landing.dae` the pad collision planes were set higher than the spot where the game places a docked ship:

- **Pad 1:** collision top 0.725 m above the locator.
- **Pads 2–6:** collision top 0.255 m above the locator.
- **Visual pad:** its landing area is level with the locator, which is why the ship looks clear of it.

So once a ship lands and is placed on its pad, its lower hull sits inside the pad's collision mesh, including the vertical struts under the pad top. The ship is then in contact with the pad while docked and as it leaves, so it takes damage. The other station models have their pads at or within a few centimetres of their locators.

**Fix:** a data-only change to that one file. All six collision pads now sit at the same height, with the top 0.10 m below the locator and the visual landing surface. I chose that small gap because a few ships' collision hulls reach a few centimetres below their landing point (up to 0.067 m for the Lodos). This covers the pad in the video and every equivalent pad on the station.

- **Ship unchanged:** no ship collision mesh or landing point was touched.
- **Landing still works:** the pad is still the highest surface under a descending ship, well above the station's own floor collision at about 69.95 m. A ship that lands still touches it and starts docking. The docking code places the ship at the locator afterwards, so it rests on the visual surface without overlapping the collision.
- **No cache:** I found no cached compiled version of the model that would override the change.

To check it, land on and lift off from any `new_ground` pad and watch that hull integrity stays at 100%.
